proposed_contract.title: Integral triangular decomposition and freeness of the Lusztig form
proposed_contract.statement: Assume AC only for the generic/classical PBW rank supplier. Over A=Z[q,q^-1], multiplication U_A^-⊗_A U_A^0⊗_A U_A^+→U_A is an isomorphism. The two divided-power halves are free A-modules with finite free root components of the classical PBW ranks. The unmodified torus has an A-basis K_c∏K_i^{delta_i}T_{i,0,t_i}, with delta_i=0 or1 and c representing Pvee/Σ Z(d_i h_i). Hence U_A is free, and the degree-beta component is ⊕_{alpha,gamma∈Q_+, alpha-gamma=beta} U_A^-[-gamma]⊗U_A^0⊗U_A^+[alpha]. Unique coefficients refer to products of chosen basis elements, not to arbitrary sums of simple tensors.
proposed_contract.strategy: Apply the simultaneous integral balanced/global construction (Kashiwara91 Sections6.1 and7.1-7.5) to U_A^-. That construction starts with an arbitrary Z[q±]-submodule and rational DVR-free chart lattices; its integral residue and height/string-ideal argument proves the actual A-basis as a conclusion. Use its negative-half global basis in each finite root degree. The unmodified integral toral-basis lemma independently supplies the full K_coset ∏K_i^delta_iT_{i,0,t_i} A-basis by Gaussian Vandermonde, toral shift/action recursions and Laurent-extremal independence. Both factors are genuinely free over the non-PID A; their tensor product with the positive half is free. Reordering gives the multiplication surjection; tensoring a kernel with Q(q) gives zero by field triangular decomposition, and the free source has no torsion, so the kernel is zero. Its homogeneous restriction gives the negative-toral-positive root decomposition. Extension to Q(q) and the published generic/classical comparison give the claimed component ranks, with AC used only in that rank supplier. No torsionfree-to-free claim over A and no modified dot-U basis is used.

proposed_contract.title: Finitely generated free integral weight lattices and deformation of the classical weight character
proposed_contract.statement: For every dominant label weight lambda, let V_A=U_Av_lambda=U_A^-v_lambda inside the simple integrable L(lambda). Over A=Z[q,q^-1], each label-weight component of V_A is finite FREE of rank dim_Q(q)L(lambda)_mu, not merely torsionfree. It spans the field module. For every characteristic-zero q=1 specialization k, the fibre has the same weight dimensions and is the classical simple integrable highest module of the explicitly regularized realization, transported to the original label lattice. Thus its character is the Weyl-Kac character (the finite Weyl character in finite type). The integral Serre quotient equals L(lambda) in every symmetrizable type, as already proved by the early local comparison.
proposed_contract.strategy: The simultaneous global construction and its based-quotient theorem give a Z[q±]-basis of U_A^-v_lambda: each negative global basis element maps to the corresponding highest-module global element if its crystal image survives, and to0 otherwise (Kashiwara91 Theorem7(ii), Section7.5.2). Thus each finite weight lattice is actually free over A, with rank its field dimension. The early local-q1 deformation/universality theorem already proves the simple quantum module, field character and equality with the integrable Serre quotient using DVR-free lattices; it is not dependent on this global result. Base change of the newly proved integral weight basis preserves dimensions. Algebraic positive specialization and finite-support regularization identify the classical fibre and its character, and the classical Weyl-Kac theorem gives the explicit formula. Perfect-pairing/regularity/fundamental-weight hypotheses used by the sources are established by the actual auxiliary-datum lemma. This proves the stronger original global Z-lattice assertion without assuming it as a balanced-triple premise.
